papers.title: The geometry of cognition: from neural populations to neurotechnology
papers.reason: Review of neural population geometry across working memory, decision-making, and cognitive variables, with clear relevance for computational models of executive function.

papers.title: Shared control-network recruitment and task-dependent brain-behavior associations in bilingual language and rule switching.
papers.reason: The title indicates a human brain-behavior study of control-network recruitment during rule switching, directly relevant to cognitive control mechanisms.

papers.title: The mediating role of early maladaptive schemas in the relationship between perceived parental attitudes and cognitive flexibility in adolescents
papers.reason: The study measures cognitive flexibility in adolescents but is primarily a psychosocial mediation analysis rather than a mechanistic or assessment-focused executive-function study.

papers.title: Challenges of war: paroxysmal disorders in military personnel. Observational experience and optimization of differential diagnosis
papers.reason: The paper focuses on differential diagnosis and treatment of epileptic versus psychogenic seizures, with only incidental mention of prefrontal inhibitory control.

papers.title: Reward-Based Eating Drive Is Associated with Distinct Resting-State Connectivity Patterns: A RED-13 and fMRI Study
papers.reason: Resting-state fMRI associations with reward-driven eating include cognitive-control regions, but the core topic is eating behavior rather than executive-function modelling or assessment.

papers.title: Neural subspaces encode sequential working memory without detectable neural sequences
papers.reason: Human MEG evidence on low-dimensional neural subspaces for sequential working memory directly informs computational models of working-memory maintenance.

papers.title: Circadian aging and neurodegeneration: the emerging role of the melatonin-cortisol axis in brain homeostasis, disease progression, and precision chronomedicine.
papers.reason: The paper appears relevant to neurodegeneration and brain health broadly but has no specific stated connection to executive-function modelling or digital cognitive assessment.

papers.title: Mechanisms and measurement of attention in laboratory tasks versus naturalistic learning contexts
papers.reason: EEG alpha oscillations are tested as neural metrics of visual attention across laboratory working memory and naturalistic learning contexts in children.

papers.title: Psychophysiological differences in stress reactivity in response to psychosocial and physiological stress in individuals with emotional burnout
papers.reason: The study combines attention, working memory, EEG, and physiological measures in a burnout sample, but its main focus is stress reactivity rather than executive-function modelling or classification.

papers.title: Assessment of the effects of psychological stress on cognitive functions and modulation of stress effects using transcranial electrical stimulation
papers.reason: The paper studies effects of acute stress and DLPFC tDCS on working memory, attention, EEG rhythms, and affective state, with moderate relevance to neural mechanisms of executive control.

papers.title: Reduced-observable dynamic mode decomposition for identifying theta and beta activity in working-memory EEG
papers.reason: Although mainly a neural time-series method paper, it is applied to working-memory EEG and recovers theta power relationships with encoding and memory load.

papers.title: Virtual Reality as a Tool for Post‑Concussion Cognitive Assessment: A Pilot Comparison of Reaction Time Metrics
papers.reason: The title indicates a VR-based clinical cognitive assessment using reaction-time metrics after concussion, but no summary is provided to establish a stronger executive-function or biomarker connection.
